tags: why do dogs chase their tail
script: Puppies chasing their own tail is usually just pure curiosity. They haven't fully connected yet that the moving thing behind them is actually part of their own body, so it becomes an accidental game. In adult dogs, tail chasing is most often boredom or excess energy looking for an outlet, basically self-entertainment when nothing else is going on. It can also show up as a play behavior that gets a laugh and attention from you, which reinforces it further. Here's the part worth knowing though. If an adult dog chases their tail obsessively, especially to the point of self-harm, that can signal anxiety or a compulsive behavior. Occasional tail chasing is totally normal play.
